narrativeReportMd:
# ActivityDefinition R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ActivityDefinition` has high-impact local breaking changes. Direct forward breaks come from removed timing choices, Reference-to-CodeableReference/canonical conversions, changed product targets, and required value-set changes for `kind` and `participant.type`.

## Scope
This report covers local ActivityDefinition elements and directly related local terminology. Inherited base-resource and datatype-internal changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The largest migration theme is movement from R4 Reference/simple-code forms toward R6 canonical, CodeableReference, richer actor, and product-definition modeling. Several paths remain the same while the wire representation changes, so path-only diffing is unsafe.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `timing[x]`, `location`, the requirement elements, `kind`, `participant.type`, and `product[x]` targets.

## Findings requiring human review
Manual review is needed for workflow code mapping, timing semantics, canonical URL resolution, product Substance migration, participant actor migration, subject canonical/reference down-conversion, and R6 as-needed preconditions.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many breaks could have been softened by retaining old choices, targets, or codes as deprecated values while adding R6 forms. The R6 direction is often semantically coherent, but official migration rationale and ConceptMaps would materially improve confidence.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: ActivityDefinition has high-impact local breaks: removed `timing[x]` choices, path-preserving wire-shape changes for `location` and requirement links, required binding changes for `kind` and `participant.type`, and changed `product[x]` reference targets. The top uncertainty is terminology migration because official expansions/ConceptMaps were not available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Focus migration on **wire-shape transforms**, **required-code validation**, and **R6-only content preservation**. Preserve unresolved references and R6-only clinical/actor data in extensions rather than silently dropping them.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural differences because both StructureDefinitions were present and inspected. Confidence is medium for exact terminology/migration semantics because local compose/code-system comparison was used without live expansions, official diffs, or ConceptMaps.

findings.title: ActivityDefinition.kind required value set removed several R4 codes and added R6 codes

oldState.summary: R4 `kind` is 0..1 code with required binding to `request-resource-types|4.0.1`; local R4 codes include AppointmentResponse, Contract, ImmunizationRecommendation, and SupplyRequest.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `kind` is 0..1 code with required binding to `request-resource-types|4.0.1`; local R4 codes include AppointmentResponse, Contract, ImmunizationRecommendation, and SupplyRequest.

newState.summary: R6 `kind` is still 0..1 code with required binding to `request-resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4`; local R6 compose omits those four R4 codes and adds CoverageEligibilityRequest and RequestOrchestration.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `kind` is still 0..1 code with required binding to `request-resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4`; local R6 compose omits those four R4 codes and adds CoverageEligibilityRequest and RequestOrchestration.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Compared local compose/code-system content, not a live expansion.

facts.newValue: R6 says kind may only specify Request resource types and recommends Task.focus for event-resource creation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The binding remains required, so an R4 instance using a removed `kind` code becomes R6-invalid. R6 instances using newly added codes cannot be represented in the R4 required value set. Generated enums and apply logic also need new and removed-code handling.

justification.inferredGoal: Constrain ActivityDefinition.kind to R6 request-resource workflow semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep removed R4 `kind` codes as deprecated or warning-only values while adding the R6 request-resource codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 comment explicitly narrows `kind` to Request resource types, and two removed R4 codes point to resources absent from the R6 package. That makes the R6 goal reasonable. A less-breaking value-set design could keep the removed codes as deprecated, but doing so would continue to validate values that R6 is trying to exclude, so the breaking choice is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would include `AppointmentResponse`, `Contract`, `ImmunizationRecommendation`, and `SupplyRequest` as deprecated or warning-only legacy codes while adding the new R6 codes. This would preserve old instances, but it would also make base R6 validators accept legacy/non-request meanings indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy instances but continues to validate legacy or removed-resource kinds in a required base value set, weakening the R6 request-only rule.

evidence.detail: Local R6 compose removes four local R4 codes and adds two R6 codes.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments include only the required `status` plus the changed field.

findings.narrativeMd: `kind` is a direct validation break because the required value set changed. Existing R4 definitions using `SupplyRequest`, `ImmunizationRecommendation`, `Contract`, or `AppointmentResponse` as the kind will fail R6 validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: removed `kind` codes are old-valid/new-invalid. R6→R4: `CoverageEligibilityRequest` and `RequestOrchestration` are not R4-valid `kind` codes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory `kind` values. Map removed codes only with workflow-specific review; otherwise preserve the original code in an extension and flag the instance.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The less disruptive alternative was to keep old codes in the value set as deprecated. That preserves validation compatibility but leaves legacy workflow states in the base model.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required binding on `ActivityDefinition.kind` changed from the R4 request-resource-types code system to an R6 value set that removes `AppointmentResponse`, `Contract`, `ImmunizationRecommendation`, and `SupplyRequest` and adds `CoverageEligibilityRequest` and `RequestOrchestration`. An R4 ActivityDefinition using a removed kind will fail R6 required-binding validation, and generated enum or apply logic must review the resource-kind switch. The R6 comment gives a coherent goal: kind is limited to Request resource types, with event creation handled through Task.focus. Because several removed choices are non-request or absent in R6, accepting them indefinitely would weaken that goal, so the break is proportionate rather than a standards issue.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition.kind is code with required binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/request-resource-types|4.0.1.
R4 CodeSystem request-resource-types includes AppointmentResponse, Contract, ImmunizationRecommendation, and SupplyRequest.

R6 ActivityDefinition.kind is code with required binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/request-resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4; the R6 value set lists CoverageEligibilityRequest and RequestOrchestration and omits those four R4 codes.
R6 kind comment says the element may only specify Request resource types and suggests Task.focus for event resources.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 ActivityDefinition is FMM 2 and trial-use, so the maturity context is neutral; the hard terminology break matters, but the request-resource rationale carries substantial weight.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a previously valid `kind` code removed from the required value set becomes R6-invalid; there is also R6-to-R4 loss for newly added request kinds.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could keep the removed codes as deprecated legacy values while adding the new R6 codes. That preserves old instances but materially weakens the R6 request-only rule and may validate resources no longer present in R6, so the alternative has real specification tradeoffs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact mechanism and partial alternative assessment; the fresh review treats the break as real but proportionate.

findings.title: ActivityDefinition.timing[x] removed dateTime and Period choices and added RelativeTime

oldState.summary: R4 allowed Timing, dateTime, Age, Period, Range, and Duration.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed Timing, dateTime, Age, Period, Range, and Duration.

newState.summary: R6 allows Timing, Age, Range, Duration, and RelativeTime; dateTime and Period are removed.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows Timing, Age, Range, Duration, and RelativeTime; dateTime and Period are removed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR choice branches are wire-level properties. R4 `timingDateTime` and `timingPeriod` are not R6 choices, while R6 `timingRelativeTime` has no R4 branch.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify definitional timing and support relative timing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `RelativeTime` while retaining `timingDateTime` and `timingPeriod` as deprecated legacy choices.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R6 explains `timing[x]` as a definitional apply-time instruction, which is a coherent reason to prefer `Age`, `Duration`, `Range`, `Timing`, and `RelativeTime` over bare `dateTime` and `Period`. Retaining the legacy choices would be less breaking, but it would keep ambiguity about whether absolute dates or periods are schedule bounds, validity windows, or apply-relative timing. With that clinical ambiguity, the break is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would add `RelativeTime` and keep `dateTime` and `Period` as deprecated or warning-only choices. This would preserve R4 instances, but it duplicates semantics already expressible through `Timing.event` or `Timing.repeat.boundsPeriod` and could keep unsafe legacy representations alive.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old wire names but leaves multiple timing representations and perpetuates absolute/period forms that are ambiguous in apply-time semantics.

evidence.detail: R6 omits dateTime/Period and includes RelativeTime.

examples.examplesMd: The Timing migration is illustrative; semantic review is needed.

findings.narrativeMd: `timing[x]` is a hard local break: two R4 wire names disappear from the R6 choice and a new R6-only datatype appears.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `timingDateTime` or `timingPeriod` are old-valid/new-invalid. R6 instances with `timingRelativeTime` cannot be represented in R4 without an extension or semantic transform.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `timingPeriod` only after deciding whether it is a schedule bound or validity window. Map `timingDateTime` to `Timing.event` only when that preserves meaning. Preserve `RelativeTime` by extension for R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping the old choices as deprecated would have preserved old data while still steering authors toward R6 timing semantics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `timingDateTime` and `timingPeriod`; R6 removes those choice branches, retains `Timing`, `Age`, `Range`, and `Duration`, and adds `RelativeTime`. This is a wire-level choice break for old instances using the removed branches and a reverse-conversion issue for `RelativeTime`. The R6 comments frame timing as an apply-time definitional instruction, which makes the removal of absolute date and period branches understandable because they are ambiguous as schedule, bounds, or validity semantics. The break is real, but the modeling goal is coherent.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition.timing[x] types are Timing, dateTime, Age, Period, Range, and Duration.
R6 ActivityDefinition.timing[x] types are Timing, Age, Range, Duration, and RelativeTime.
R6 timing comment explains interpretation during apply operations and describes Age, Duration, Range, and Timing semantics.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral here; it does not erase the choice-type break, but it also does not create a high stability burden beyond the path-level mechanism.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `timingDateTime` and `timingPeriod` properties are not R6 choice branches; R6 `timingRelativeTime` has no R4 branch.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained dateTime and Period as deprecated choices while adding RelativeTime. That would preserve old wire forms, but it would keep multiple partially overlapping timing representations and preserve the ambiguity R6 appears to be removing.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact mechanism and partial alternative assessment.

findings.title: ActivityDefinition.location changed from Reference(Location) to CodeableReference(Location)

oldState.summary: R4 `location` is an optional Reference targeting Location.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `location` is an optional Reference targeting Location.

newState.summary: R6 `location` is an optional CodeableReference targeting Location.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `location` is an optional CodeableReference targeting Location.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The path is stable but Reference and CodeableReference are not wire-compatible. R6 can also carry a coded concept with no R4 base equivalent.

justification.inferredGoal: Support either a specific Location or coded location type.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `location` as `Reference(Location)` and add an optional coded-location sibling for location type concepts.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: `CodeableReference(Location)` directly models the R4 comment that the location may be either a specific location or a type of location. A sibling coded element would have avoided invalidating existing `Reference`-shaped instances, but it would duplicate the same fact and make conflict handling a permanent base-model concern. The breaking design is therefore probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would retain the R4 `location` Reference and add a separate coded location/type element. This preserves existing instances and supports coded locations, but systems would need rules for cases where both fields are populated or disagree, and the duplicate representation could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids the wrapping break but creates duplicate places to represent the same location fact and possible conflicts between reference and concept.

findings.narrativeMd: `location` is a path-preserving but wire-incompatible change that affects parsers, serializers, FHIRPath expressions, and generated classes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Reference-shaped `location` is invalid as R6 CodeableReference. R6 `location.reference` can be unwrapped to R4, but R6 `location.concept` has no R4 base field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 Reference values under `CodeableReference.reference`. Preserve R6 concepts in extensions or require manual mapping to a concrete Location for R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A choice or additional element would have avoided invalidating existing Reference-shaped instances, at the cost of a less uniform R6 model.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `ActivityDefinition.location` keeps the same path and cardinality but changes from `Reference(Location)` to `CodeableReference(Location)`. Existing R4 JSON using a bare Reference object is not the R6 CodeableReference shape, and generated models change from a reference property to a concept-or-reference wrapper. The R6 type directly addresses the R4 comment that location may identify either a specific location or a location type. The compatibility cost is significant but proportionate to avoiding parallel location representations.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition.location is 0..1 Reference targeting Location.
R6 ActivityDefinition.location is 0..1 CodeableReference targeting Location.
Both R4 and R6 comments state that the element may reference a specific clinical location or identify a type of location.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral; the direct wire-shape break counts, but the model-improvement rationale can justify it.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Reference-shaped `location` is not the R6 CodeableReference wrapper; generated APIs also change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have kept `location` as Reference and added a coded location/type sibling. That would preserve old instances but create duplicate places for the same fact and require conflict rules when both are populated.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact mechanism and partial alternative assessment.

findings.title: Specimen and observation requirement elements changed from Reference arrays to canonical arrays

oldState.summary: R4 requirement elements are 0..* Reference values to SpecimenDefinition or ObservationDefinition.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 requirement elements are 0..* Reference values to SpecimenDefinition or ObservationDefinition.

newState.summary: R6 requirement elements are 0..* canonical values targeting SpecimenDefinition or ObservationDefinition.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 requirement elements are 0..* canonical values targeting SpecimenDefinition or ObservationDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Reference objects and canonical primitive strings have incompatible wire shapes. Conversion also requires resolving references to canonical URLs and may lose display/identifier information.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent definitional dependencies by canonical URL.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the Reference requirement arrays and add parallel canonical requirement elements for definitional dependencies.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Canonical URLs are a better fit for reusable definitional resources such as `SpecimenDefinition` and `ObservationDefinition`, so the R6 goal is reasonable. A transition design could have retained the Reference arrays, but it would create parallel representations for the same dependency and would not guarantee that references can be resolved to stable canonicals. The break is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep the R4 Reference elements and add canonical siblings, with guidance to prefer the canonical form. That would preserve R4 instances but at the cost of duplicate same-resource representations, ambiguity when both forms are present, and continued implementation burden for reference resolution.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old arrays but duplicates dependency links and forces validators and converters to reconcile references, canonicals, and unresolved targets.

evidence.locator: snapshot elements for specimenRequirement and observationRequirement
snapshot elements for specimenRequirement and observationRequirement

findings.narrativeMd: The three requirement links retain names and cardinalities but change to a different wire representation, making existing R4 arrays invalid in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Reference arrays are old-valid/new-invalid. R6 canonical arrays require constructing R4 References on down-conversion and may not resolve losslessly.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Resolve each R4 Reference to the target resource canonical URL; preserve unresolved references in extensions. For R6→R4, generate References only when a target endpoint or local resource is known.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A choice type or parallel canonical fields would have avoided breaking existing Reference-shaped data while encouraging canonical use.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `specimenRequirement`, `observationRequirement`, and `observationResultRequirement` changed from arrays of Reference objects to arrays of canonical primitives. R4 instances that point to contained or external definitional resources by Reference must be transformed, and migration may require resolving a reference to the target resource canonical URL. For definitional dependencies on SpecimenDefinition and ObservationDefinition, canonical URLs are the better R6 base representation, so the break is substantial but justified.
keyEvidence: R4 specimenRequirement is Reference(SpecimenDefinition), and observationRequirement and observationResultRequirement are Reference(ObservationDefinition).
R6 specimenRequirement is canonical(SpecimenDefinition), and observationRequirement and observationResultRequirement are canonical(ObservationDefinition).
The element definitions continue to describe reusable specimen and observation requirements for the action.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral; the wire-shape break matters, but the affected paths are definitional dependency links where canonical references are a coherent R6 direction.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 Reference array entries are incompatible with R6 canonical strings, and conversion can require resolving a reference and losing display or identifier details.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained Reference arrays and added canonical siblings or a broader choice shape. That would preserve old instances but duplicate dependency representations and force validators and converters to reconcile references, canonicals, and unresolved targets.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact mechanism and partial alternative assessment.

findings.title: ActivityDefinition.product[x] Reference targets removed Substance and added R6 product-definition resources

oldState.summary: R4 productReference targets Medication or Substance; productCodeableConcept remains available.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 productReference targets Medication or Substance; productCodeableConcept remains available.

newState.summary: R6 productReference targets Medication, MedicinalProductDefinition, Ingredient, or SubstanceDefinition; productCodeableConcept remains available.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 productReference targets Medication, MedicinalProductDefinition, Ingredient, or SubstanceDefinition; productCodeableConcept remains available.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A R4 productReference to Substance violates the R6 target profile. R6 references to new product-definition resources do not fit the R4 target list.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Substance` as a deprecated `productReference` target while adding the new R6 product-definition targets.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 product-definition direction is reasonable, but `Substance` still exists in the R6 package and could have remained an allowed deprecated target while the new targets were added. That would preserve R4-valid `productReference` instances with a low to moderate long-term tradeoff, so the target removal was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backwards-compatible base design would widen the R6 target list to include `Medication`, `Substance`, `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `Ingredient`, and `SubstanceDefinition`, marking `Substance` as legacy or deprecated where appropriate. This preserves old instances while still enabling the newer product-definition model; the cost is slower migration away from the less precise legacy target.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Allows less precise legacy `Substance` references to remain valid, but does not introduce a new field or wire-shape ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 Reference targets Medication and Substance.
R6 Reference targets Medication, MedicinalProductDefinition, Ingredient, SubstanceDefinition.

findings.narrativeMd: `product[x]` keeps the same Reference wire shape but changes target validity, which affects validators and type-safe reference handling.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Substance targets are old-valid/new-invalid. New R6 targets are not R4-representable except by extension, CodeableConcept fallback, or manual mapping.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map Substance only when a reliable SubstanceDefinition/Ingredient equivalent exists; otherwise preserve the original reference.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Retaining Substance as an allowed but deprecated target would have avoided the R4→R6 validation break.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `product[x]` allowed `productReference` to Medication or Substance; R6 keeps Medication and CodeableConcept but removes Substance while adding MedicinalProductDefinition, Ingredient, and SubstanceDefinition. A valid R4 ActivityDefinition that points to a Substance product is therefore rejected by the R6 target profile. The R6 product-definition direction is reasonable, but Substance still exists in the R6 package, and retaining it as a legacy target would preserve old instances without introducing a second field or wire-shape conflict. This looks like an avoidable hard target-list break.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition.product[x] is Reference(Medication, Substance) or CodeableConcept.
R6 ActivityDefinition.product[x] is Reference(Medication, MedicinalProductDefinition, Ingredient, SubstanceDefinition) or CodeableConcept.
R6 package contains StructureDefinition-Substance.json, so the removed R4 target resource still exists.
R6 package also contains the new MedicinalProductDefinition, Ingredient, and SubstanceDefinition targets.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral, so the decision turns on the path-level break and alternatives; the avoidable target removal is still concerning.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `productReference` to Substance no longer satisfies the R6 target list; R6 references to new product-definition targets are also not R4-representable.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A low-cost less-breaking base design exists: retain Substance as a deprecated or legacy Reference target while adding the newer product-definition targets. The tradeoff is slower migration away from a less precise target, but it avoids a hard break without duplicate fields.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact and less-breaking-alternative-available assessment.

findings.title: ActivityDefinition participant typing changed required codes and added R6-only actor fields

oldState.summary: R4 participant.type is 1..1 with required action-participant-type codes patient, practitioner, related-person, and device.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 participant.type is 1..1 with required action-participant-type codes patient, practitioner, related-person, and device.

newState.summary: R6 participant.type is 0..1 with a required binding containing ten codes; R4 `related-person` is absent and R6 adds typeCanonical, typeReference, and function.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 participant.type is 0..1 with a required binding containing ten codes; R4 `related-person` is absent and R6 adds typeCanonical, typeReference, and function.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The required binding no longer accepts the R4 code `related-person`. R6 also allows participants without the R4-required `type`, or with typeCanonical/typeReference/function data that R4 cannot represent.

justification.inferredGoal: Align participant typing with more R6 actor resources and functions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `related-person` as a deprecated alias for `relatedperson` while adding the broader R6 actor fields and codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The broader R6 participant actor model is reasonable, but the hard R4-to-R6 break is mainly the removal of the old `related-person` code spelling. Keeping that spelling as a deprecated alias would preserve R4 instances while still permitting `relatedperson`, `typeCanonical`, `typeReference`, and `function`. Because the tradeoff is manageable, this break was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would include both `related-person` and `relatedperson` in the required value set, with clear deprecation and normalization guidance for the old spelling. This does not solve every R6-to-R4 issue from the new actor fields, but it directly avoids the R4-to-R6 validation break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Creates two spellings for the RelatedPerson concept and a normalization burden, but preserves R4 instances without blocking the R6 actor model.

evidence.detail: R4 min is 1 and binding is action-participant-type|4.0.1.
R6 min is 0 and binding is action-participant-type|6.0.0-ballot4.

findings.narrativeMd: `participant` changed in two related ways: a required code set changed, and R6 added richer actor typing surfaces. The code `related-person` is a hard R4→R6 validation break; the added fields are major R6→R4 risks.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: `participant.type = related-person` is old-valid/new-invalid. R6→R4: participants can omit `type` or use new actor fields, violating R4 cardinality or losing detail.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `related-person` to `relatedperson` only after confirming policy or a ConceptMap. For R6 actor fields, infer a safe R4 type where possible and preserve exact actor/function data in extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new model could have been additive if R6 retained the old code spelling and kept a required coarse type.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 participant model required `participant.type` and its required value set included `related-person`. R6 makes `type` optional, adds typeCanonical, typeReference, and function, and changes the RelatedPerson code spelling to `relatedperson`. The optionality decrease and new actor fields are not R4-to-R6 hard breaks, but a valid R4 participant with type `related-person` becomes invalid under the R6 required binding. Keeping the old spelling as a deprecated alias would avoid the direct break while still allowing the richer R6 actor model.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition.participant.type is min 1, code, required binding to action-participant-type|4.0.1.
R4 action-participant-type codes are device, patient, practitioner, and related-person.
R6 ActivityDefinition.participant.type is min 0 with required binding to action-participant-type|6.0.0-ballot4.

R6 action-participant-type replaces related-person with relatedperson and adds careteam, group, healthcareservice, location, organization, and practitionerrole; R6 also adds typeCanonical, typeReference, and function.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral, but the direct required-code spelling break has a modest, plausible base-compatible fix.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `participant.type = related-person` fails the R6 required binding; the new R6 actor fields mainly create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could include both `related-person` and `relatedperson` in the required value set, with deprecation and normalization guidance for the old spelling. The cost is a temporary alias and normalization burden, but that is modest compared with the hard validation break.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact and less-breaking-alternative-available assessment, while treating the spelling break as the main R4-to-R6 concern.

findings.title: ActivityDefinition.subject[x] expanded references and added canonical subject with a different extensible binding

oldState.summary: R4 subject[x] allows CodeableConcept or Reference(Group), with extensible binding to subject-type.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 subject[x] allows CodeableConcept or Reference(Group), with extensible binding to subject-type.

newState.summary: R6 subject[x] allows CodeableConcept, Reference(Group plus pharmaceutical definition resources), and canonical(EvidenceVariable), with extensible binding to participant-resource-types.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 subject[x] allows CodeableConcept, Reference(Group plus pharmaceutical definition resources), and canonical(EvidenceVariable), with extensible binding to participant-resource-types.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The change is mostly additive for R4→R6, but R6 subjectCanonical and new reference targets have no R4 base representation. The binding is extensible, so it is less likely to produce hard validation failures.

justification.inferredGoal: Support pharmaceutical-quality and EvidenceVariable subject definitions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 because the R6 subject changes are additive and R4 subject forms remain valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R6 widens `subject[x]` by adding canonical and product-definition subject forms while retaining the R4 `CodeableConcept` and `Reference(Group)` forms. The supplied R6 comment even cautions limited use of the new canonical form for backward compatibility. Since this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue, the additive design is justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Standard R4 extensions or down-conversion policies may be needed for `subjectCanonical` and the new reference targets, but those are R6-to-R4 mitigations. They should not be counted as backwards-compatible base R6 alternatives because existing R4 instances already remain representable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The main cost is R6-to-R4 preservation of new canonical and product-subject forms, which requires mapping or extensions rather than a base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds canonical and pharmaceutical references and includes backward-compatibility caution.

findings.narrativeMd: `subject[x]` is not a forward hard break but is a notable R6→R4 and codegen risk because it adds a new choice branch and several new reference targets.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 subject values remain structurally valid in R6. R6 `subjectCanonical` and new target references are not R4-representable without extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve R6 subjectCanonical and pharmaceutical target references with explicit extensions when producing R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additive change is forward-compatible; the main missing compatibility aid is standardized down-conversion guidance.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens `subject[x]` rather than narrowing it. The R4 forms, CodeableConcept and Reference(Group), remain available, and the binding remains extensible. R6 adds product-definition reference targets and canonical(EvidenceVariable), with an explicit comment recommending limited use of the new canonical form for backward compatibility. The practical issue is preserving new R6 subject forms when converting backward to R4, not accepting old R4 content in R6.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition.subject[x] types are CodeableConcept and Reference(Group).
R6 ActivityDefinition.subject[x] retains CodeableConcept and Reference(Group), adds additional product-definition reference targets, and adds canonical(EvidenceVariable).
R4 subject binding is extensible to subject-type; R6 binding is extensible to participant-resource-types.
R6 comment says canonical was introduced to support pharmaceutical quality use cases and recommends limited use for backward compatibility.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral, but there is no meaningful R4-to-R6 break to amplify.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: new R6 subjectCanonical and new reference targets may need extensions or mapping when downgrading, but R4 subject forms remain valid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the old choices are retained. Backward conversion policy or extensions may still be useful for R6-only forms.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing finding facts and reverse-conversion concern, but downweight it to No problem because the R4-to-R6 base path is additive.

findings.title: ActivityDefinition.intent required binding added R6 intent codes and changed some definitions

oldState.summary: R4 intent is 0..1 code with required binding to request-intent|4.0.1.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 intent is 0..1 code with required binding to request-intent|4.0.1.

newState.summary: R6 intent is 0..1 code with required binding to request-intent|6.0.0-ballot4 and adds solicit-offer and offer-response.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 intent is 0..1 code with required binding to request-intent|6.0.0-ballot4 and adds solicit-offer and offer-response.

newValue: directive no longer says legally binding
order now says requestor rather than Practitioner

impact.impactRationaleMd: Local R6 terminology retains R4 codes, so existing R4 instances should validate. R6 adds codes and semantic definition changes that R4 enum switches and business rules will not understand.

justification.inferredGoal: Support solicitation/offer workflows and R6 RequestOrchestration semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because R4 intent codes remain valid and the R6 terminology change is additive for existing instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 code system adds solicitation and offer-response workflow concepts while retaining the R4 intent codes. Existing R4 instances are therefore not invalidated by the added codes, although business logic may need semantic review because some definitions changed. The goal is reasonable and the R4-to-R6 base compatibility alternative question is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Cross-version ConceptMaps and migration notes are useful mitigations for R6-to-R4 conversion and runtime rules, but they are not base-design alternatives. For R4-to-R6 validation, the less-breaking design is already achieved by retaining the old codes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-only intent codes and changed definitions still need mapping and business-rule review for down-conversion, but that is not a less-breaking base R6 design.

findings.narrativeMd: `intent` is an additive terminology change for R4→R6 but a round-trip and business-rule risk for systems that treat intent as authority or workflow state.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 `solicit-offer` and `offer-response` cannot be represented in R4. Existing code definitions also changed in ways that may affect authorization logic.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update enums and business rules. Preserve new R6 intent codes in extensions or reject R6→R4 conversion when intent is clinically/business critical.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The code additions themselves are forward-compatible; the compatibility need is explicit mapping and semantic documentation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The `intent` required binding changes versions, but R6 retains the R4 intent codes and adds more specific R6 workflow codes such as order specializations, solicit-offer, and offer-response. Existing R4 instances using proposal, plan, directive, order, or option remain valid. Some business logic and generated enums should review the new values and definition shifts, but that is primarily an R6-to-R4 or new-R6-content concern rather than a break for R4 content moving to R6.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition.intent is code with required binding to request-intent|4.0.1.
R6 ActivityDefinition.intent is code with required binding to request-intent|6.0.0-ballot4.
R6 request-intent CodeSystem retains proposal, plan, directive, order, and option.
R6 request-intent adds concepts including original-order, reflex-order, filler-order, instance-order, solicit-offer, and offer-response.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral; because the required binding is additive for existing R4 codes, maturity does not create a standards concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6-only intent codes and some changed definitions may need mapping for older systems, but existing R4 codes are still accepted in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is needed for R4-to-R6 validation because the old codes are retained. ConceptMaps or migration notes can help with R6-to-R4 and business-rule review, but those are not base R6 alternatives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-conversion and runtime concern, but classify it as No problem for R4-to-R6 compatibility.

findings.title: ActivityDefinition.usage primitive type changed from string to markdown

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON primitive shape remains string-like, so ordinary values are unlikely to become invalid. Generated primitive classes, rendering, sanitization, and UI behavior can still change.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer formatted clinical usage guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `usage` typed as `string` and state in the definition or guidance that markdown syntax is allowed or expected.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Changing from `string` to `markdown` is low impact for JSON instance compatibility but can affect generated models and UI rendering. Keeping `string` with prose guidance would be less disruptive, but it would only partially meet the R6 goal because consumers could not reliably detect markdown semantics from the base type. The change is therefore probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would retain the R4 `string` type and strengthen the definition, comments, or best-practice guidance to say that markdown content may be used. This preserves old code generation, but it relies on prose rather than a computable primitive type and gives weaker support for safe rendering and sanitization.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids generated-type churn but loses the computable primitive-type signal for markdown rendering, sanitization, and validation expectations.

examples.examplesMd: No concrete instance fragment is needed beyond the structured old/new state.

findings.narrativeMd: `usage` is mainly a code-generation and rendering change rather than a hard instance break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 strings should generally remain acceptable as R6 markdown. R6 markdown can be copied to R4 as a string but formatting semantics may be lost.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated models and UI rendering/sanitization; test primitive extensions on `_usage`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping string would have avoided codegen churn but would not communicate formatting semantics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `ActivityDefinition.usage` changes from the FHIR `string` primitive to `markdown`. Plain R4 string values remain JSON-string-shaped and should normally be acceptable as markdown content, so this is not a hard instance-validation break for ordinary data. The real compatibility concern is generated model types, rendering, and sanitization behavior: consumers may now treat the text as markdown instead of plain text. That is a real but low-burden API and UI migration, and the computable markdown signal is a reasonable R6 goal.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition.usage is 0..1 string.
R6 ActivityDefinition.usage is 0..1 markdown.
The definition text remains a detailed description of how the activity definition is used from a clinical perspective.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral; it supports treating this as a small proportionate codegen and rendering migration rather than a standards issue.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: the JSON primitive remains string-like, but generated primitive classes and UI rendering or sanitization expectations can change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `usage` as string and used prose to allow markdown. That would reduce generated-type churn but would not provide a computable primitive-type signal for markdown-aware rendering and safety handling.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact and partial alternative assessment; the fresh judgment recognizes a real but proportionate codegen and rendering break.

findings.title: R6 adds ActivityDefinition.asNeeded[x] clinical precondition with no R4 base equivalent

newState.summary: R6 adds optional asNeeded[x] as boolean or CodeableConcept with example medication-as-needed-reason binding.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional asNeeded[x] as boolean or CodeableConcept with example medication-as-needed-reason binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate R4 instances in R6, but R6 as-needed clinical preconditions are not representable in R4 and strict R4 parsers reject the unknown property.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 alternative is needed because `asNeeded[x]` is an optional additive R6 element and does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: `asNeeded[x]` adds useful optional clinical precondition semantics. Because absent optional content preserves all R4 instances in R6, the base-design breakage question is not applicable and the addition is justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using a standard extension for R4 export is appropriate migration guidance for R6-to-R4 conversion, but it is not a backwards-compatible base R6 design alternative. The R6 base model already uses the compatibility-preserving approach for R4-to-R6 by making the element optional.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 loss must be handled by an extension or conversion policy; that is a down-conversion mitigation, not a base R6 alternative.

findings.narrativeMd: `asNeeded[x]` is forward-compatible but important for R6→R4 because dropping it can change when an activity is performed.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6 is safe by absence. R6→R4 requires extension or loss of clinical precondition information.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve asNeededBoolean/asNeededCodeableConcept in a documented extension for R4 and do not silently drop it in order-generation contexts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The optional base addition is reasonable; the compatibility gap is lack of a built-in R4 element.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `asNeeded[x]` with boolean and CodeableConcept choices. Because the element did not exist in R4 and is optional in R6, no R4 instance is invalidated when moving forward. The only meaningful concern is that R6 instances using the new precondition cannot be represented directly in base R4, which is a normal reverse-conversion issue for an additive element.
keyEvidence: R4 ActivityDefinition has no ActivityDefinition.asNeeded[x] element.
R6 ActivityDefinition.asNeeded[x] is 0..1 and allows boolean or CodeableConcept.
R6 asNeeded[x] binding is example strength to medication-as-needed-reason.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral, and the additive optional design does not create an R4-to-R6 stability concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 as-needed precondition data needs an extension or conversion policy for R4, but old R4 content remains valid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base alternative is needed because optional addition is already compatibility-preserving for R4-to-R6. R4 extensions are migration mitigations, not base R6 alternatives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-conversion concern, but classify it as No problem because the R4-to-R6 base change is purely additive.

findings.title: R6 adds or strengthens warning constraints on ActivityDefinition name, url, and relatedArtifact

oldState.summary: R4 had local root warning adf-0 for machine-friendly name; no local url or relatedArtifact warnings were present on these paths.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had local root warning adf-0 for machine-friendly name; no local url or relatedArtifact warnings were present on these paths.

newState.summary: R6 uses cnl-0 for name, adds cnl-1 URL warning, and adds adf-2/adf-3 relatedArtifact warnings.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses cnl-0 for name, adds cnl-1 URL warning, and adds adf-2/adf-3 relatedArtifact warnings.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These are warning-severity constraints, so they should not make instances invalid under normal policy. They can still break publication or CI pipelines that treat warnings as errors.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve canonical-resource and dependency modeling quality.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base alternative is needed because R6 uses warning-severity constraints rather than making the content invalid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 constraints improve canonical-resource and related-artifact quality while remaining warning severity. That is already a compatibility-preserving base design: existing content may receive new warnings, but it is not made invalid by the base specification. The change is justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-disruptive base approach is already present: keep these checks as warnings. Suppressing the warnings entirely would weaken QA, while treating them as fatal is an implementation or publication-policy choice rather than a base R6 alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Compatibility risk comes from local tooling that promotes warnings to errors, not from an unavoidable base validation break.

evidence.detail: R6 URL warning against |, #, and spaces.

examples.examplesMd: This is warning-producing content, not necessarily invalid content.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 warning constraints do not create hard validation breaks but can affect QA and publication workflows.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Instances with single-character names, URLs containing `|` or `#`, or composed-of related artifacts may receive new R6 warnings. They remain valid unless local tooling fails on warnings.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Run R6 validation in warning-reporting mode first; normalize URLs and review relatedArtifact use before making warnings fatal.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping these as warnings is the compatibility-preserving design; the risk comes from downstream enforcement policy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The relevant R6 constraints are warning severity: cnl-0 for machine-usable names, cnl-1 for canonical URLs without problematic characters, and adf-2/adf-3 for relatedArtifact quality. Warning-as-error pipelines may need policy updates or content cleanup, but the base R6 StructureDefinition is not making old instances invalid. Using warnings is already the compatibility-preserving way to express these quality expectations.

R6 root has warning cnl-0 for ActivityDefinition.name.
R6 ActivityDefinition.url has warning cnl-1 against |, #, and spaces.

freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 trial-use is neutral; because the constraints are warning-level only, maturity does not turn them into a base compatibility problem.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: warning-level: local tooling that treats warnings as errors can fail, but ordinary base validation does not reject the instances.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base alternative is needed. Suppressing the warnings would weaken quality guidance, while escalating them to errors would be more breaking; warning severity is the compatibility-preserving compromise.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact and not-applicable alternative assessment.
